summary.headline: J. Kumar Infraprojects Q2 FY27 revenue rose 15% to ₹1,539 crore, order book stands at ₹22,711 crore, with H2 order inflow guided at ₹8,000–10,000 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations up 15% YoY to ₹1,539 crore, with Q2 profit up 18% to ₹229 crore (as stated) and PAT up 25% to ₹113 crore; Q2 operating margin was 14.9% vs 14.5% a year earlier. H1 revenue rose 8% to ₹3,050 crore and H1 EBITDA-type profit rose 8% to ₹443 crore, with H1 PAT up 9% to ₹221 crore. Net cash stood at ₹69 crore at 30 September, and working capital days were 100 vs 99 a year earlier. Management reiterated a 15% FY27 revenue growth target, implying about ₹6,500 crore, and a ₹10,000 crore revenue ambition for FY28/FY30 (the call is inconsistent on the year).

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Metro 7%, elevated corridors 47%, road tunnels 19%, others 26% of ₹22,711 crore order book, as stated in the call (the 7% and 47% figures are as transcribed and may be misstated).

segments.name: Tunnel boring machines (metro)
segments.commentary: 7 TBMs for metro; 4 currently in execution at Delhi, with the rest freeing up after Surat and Delhi work completes and needing refurbishment before redeployment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of about 15%, implying about ₹6,500 crore; H1 growth was 8%, so H2 must grow sharply.
Q3 FY27 revenue expected to rise sequentially by at least ₹100–150 crore over Q2's ₹1,536 crore; management said it would be higher than that.
H2 FY27 order inflow expected at ₹8,000–10,000 crore for the full year, with ₹5,540 crore already won in H1 (as stated).
Operating margin of 14–15% currently; target 15–16% in one to two years on the path to ₹10,000 crore revenue.
FY27 depreciation to step up from Q3 after the Thane-area tunnel (TVN) commissioning; Q3 depreciation estimated at about ₹50–52 crore vs ₹47 crore in Q2 (as stated).
FY27 capex expected at about ₹150 crore, broadly unchanged; Q2 capex about ₹80 crore.
capex_capacity: Vadhvan port project mobilised; excavation, ground clearing and survey done; execution to ramp from January.
GMLR: about 70–75% of foundation work complete, around 2,900 precast segments cast; completion targeted December 2027 / January 2028.
Verliz–Shivri connector and Shivri–Navi Mumbai airport connector expected to complete in calendar 2027; Metro Line 2B extension to Bandra also expected in 2027.
Metro bid pipeline: about ₹3,000 crore of bids submitted; about ₹30,000 crore expected to be bid within six months (elevated corridors/roads ~₹10,000 crore, metros and buildings ~₹5,000 crore).
Delhi Metro L1 order was cancelled due to project change and cost increase; a limited re-tender among existing bidders expected in 10–15 days.
demand_pricing: Management described bidding competition as intense but cyclical; new PQ norms from MoRTH are tightening, which should reduce competition in niche projects.
Company is exploring HAM projects (NHAI only), with equity commitments possibly around ₹100–200 crore per project; primary focus remains EPC.
Management said it bids at margin and is not chasing orders at any rate; Adani was described as focused on BOT rather than EPC.
Labour: management said no serious shortage, with increased use of casting and mechanised methods to reduce labour needs.
Collections: about ₹1,500 crore billed as of 30 Sep with about ₹900 crore received by the call date, leaving about ₹600 crore pending (as stated).

qa_highlights.question: Q3 revenue outlook and FY27 growth path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q3 to be higher than Q2 by at least ₹100–150 crore and reiterated 15% FY27 growth; H1 growth was 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Order inflow visibility for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹5,540 crore won in H1; H2 inflows of ₹8,000–10,000 crore for the full year, with a ₹30,000 crore bid pipeline over six months.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital, mobilisation advance, retention and unbilled revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mobilisation advance ₹627 crore, unbilled revenue ₹572 crore, security deposits ₹490 crore as of the call date; working capital cycle about 100 days, within the 100–120 day band.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold large free FDs with net cash only ₹69 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FDs are needed for bank guarantees and bid margin money; management did not give the exact free FD amount (an analyst cited ~₹700 crore) and said debt is mainly working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of China TBM export restrictions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said China accounts for under 10% of TBMs in India; assembly was shifted and TBM supply is regular, with the GMLR machine delayed by one to two months.

qa_highlights.question: Labour shortage and tunnel boring machine utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no serious labour issue; 4 of 7 metro TBMs are in execution at Delhi, with the rest to be redeployed after 6–12 months of refurbishment.

risks_watch: H1 growth of 8% vs full-year 15% target needs a steep H2 ramp; Q1 was roughly flat and H1 is well below target.
Order inflow depends on converting ₹30,000 crore of bids; the Delhi Metro L1 award was cancelled and re-tender is pending.
Depreciation rises from Q3 with TVN commissioning, which may pressure margins.
Pledge on shares with the main bank for working capital limits remains unreleased; management has requested release.
Pending SEBI-related matter; management said documents were submitted and the matter is procedural, with no timeline given.
Management referred to a higher volume of unpaid receivables and a monetisation target of about ₹180 crore (as stated), with delivery still to be confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and collections, but vague on specifics: several figures were restated, and questions on the free FD balance, FY28 breakdown and exact depreciation were deferred to the financial team.
key_quotes: We are not like thirsty for orders you know so we don't put project at any rate.
So by God's grace we don't see any issues in collecting the payments all of our payments are coming on time.
We are looking for an operating margin like right now we are at 14 to 15% so we are trying to take it 100 basis point up in the range of 15 to 16%.

adds.what: 7 metro TBMs (tunnel boring machines); 4 in execution at Delhi, rest to be redeployed after Surat/Delhi work and refurbishment

growth.why: Management reiterated about 15% FY27 revenue growth (~₹6,500 crore), but H1 growth was only 8%, so H2 must grow sharply; backing is a ₹22,711 crore order book and H2 inflow guidance of ₹8,000–10,000 crore, with ₹5,540 crore already won in H1, while the specific new capacity is limited to TBM redeployment and project timelines (GMLR Dec 2027/Jan 2028, Vadhvan ramp from January).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating margin 14.9% in Q2 vs 14.5% a year ago; management targets 15-16% in one to two years, though depreciation steps up from Q3 with TVN commissioning (~₹50-52 cr vs ₹47 cr in Q2).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant capex, but Vadhvan ramps from January, Verliz-Shivri and Navi Mumbai connectors complete in calendar 2027, and GMLR targets Dec 2027/Jan 2028; 7 metro TBMs with 4 in use at Delhi, rest to be redeployed after 6-12 months refurbishment.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterates ~15% FY27 growth (~₹6,500 cr), but H1 grew only 8% (₹3,050 cr), so H2 must rise sharply; Q3 guided at least ₹100-150 cr above Q2's ₹1,536 cr, backed by ₹22,711 cr order book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex held at ~₹150 cr (Q2 ~₹80 cr) and the call gave no utilisation figure; the HAM equity commitment of ₹100-200 cr per project is exploratory, not firm.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of ~15% is held, but H1 growth was only 8%, so a raise is not credible; the FY28 ₹10,000 cr ambition was stated inconsistently (FY28/FY30).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 growth of 8% vs a 15% FY27 target requires a steep H2 ramp, and H2 order inflow of ₹8,000-10,000 cr depends on converting ₹30,000 cr of bids after the Delhi Metro L1 cancellation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or models discussed.

rows.label: H2 order inflow of ₹8,000-10,000 cr
rows.why: ₹5,540 cr already won in H1, so H2 needs roughly ₹2,500-4,500 cr more; conversion of ~₹30,000 cr bid pipeline is uncertain and the Delhi Metro L1 was cancelled with a re-tender pending.

rows.label: Collections and pledge release
rows.why: About ₹900 cr of ₹1,500 cr billed was received, leaving ~₹600 cr pending; working capital days at 100 (vs 99), and bank pledge release is still unreleased.

rows.label: New MoRTH PQ norms reducing competition
rows.why: Management says tighter PQ norms should reduce competition in niche projects, but bidding remains intense and the company bids at margin.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 15% FY27 target, collections and margins, but vague on the H2 ramp, free FD balance and depreciation; analysts pressed on the free FDs (~₹700 cr cited), the H1 8% growth versus the 15% target, and the China TBM impact.

quality.why: Q2 revenue rose 15% to ₹1,539 crore but the brief does not say whether volume or price drove it, gives no volume growth figure, and lists no one-off items; H1 revenue growth was only 8%, and the Q2 profit and PAT figures are internally inconsistent in the brief.
